content: Sodium alginate is the sodium salt derived from alginic acid. Its chemical formula is NaC6H7O6. When extracted from the cell walls of brown algae, it takes the form of a gum. This gum is widely utilized in the food industry to enhance viscosity and act as an emulsifier. Additionally, sodium alginate is employed in the formulation of indigestion tablets and in the preparation of dental impressions. It is noteworthy that sodium alginate is devoid of any discernible flavor. Another significant application of sodium alginate is in the textile industry, where it is used in reactive dye printing processes. Sodium alginate also exhibits chelating properties, making it effective in removing radioactive toxins such as iodine-131 and strontium-90 from the body. These radioactive elements often replace their non-radioactive counterparts in biological systems. Furthermore, sodium alginate is utilized in the immobilization of enzymes through inclusion techniques.
